learningObjectives.title: Early models of the solar system

options: Backwards (westward) loop of a planet against the stars
questions.explain: Planets occasionally appear to move backwards against the stars; the heliocentric model explains this as an overtaking effect.

questions.q: Tycho Brahe is best remembered for:
options: Making very accurate naked-eye observations of the planets
questions.explain: Tycho Brahe's precise pre-telescope observations gave Kepler the data to find his laws.

questions.q: Whose law of universal gravitation explained why the planets follow Kepler's laws?
questions.explain: Newton's law of gravitation provided the underlying force explaining Kepler's planetary laws.

questions.q: Galileo's observation of the phases of Venus provided evidence that:
questions.explain: The full set of Venus's phases can only occur if Venus orbits the Sun, supporting heliocentrism.

questions.q: The heliocentric model proposed by Copernicus placed which body at the centre?
questions.explain: Copernicus placed the Sun at the centre, with the planets including Earth orbiting it.

questions.q: Which astronomer used the newly invented telescope to discover the four large moons of Jupiter?
questions.explain: Galileo's telescopic discovery of Jupiter's moons showed not everything orbits the Earth.

questions.q: Which astronomer worked out the three laws of planetary motion using precise observational data?
questions.explain: Kepler derived his three laws of planetary motion, including elliptical orbits.

questions.q: The geocentric model of the universe placed which body at the centre?
questions.explain: In the geocentric (Ptolemaic) model the Earth was at the centre with everything orbiting it.

questions.q: A major weakness of the Ptolemaic (geocentric) model was that:
options: It placed the Sun at the centre
It was never used by anyone
It needed complex epicycles to explain planetary motion
questions.explain: The geocentric model required elaborate epicycles to match observed planetary motions.

questions.q: Which of these correctly orders the astronomers from earliest to latest?
questions.explain: Ptolemy (ancient) came first, then Copernicus, Kepler and finally Newton.
